hints: Focus on the general rule for Group 2 nitrates, they always decompose to the metal oxide plus nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.
Notice that the nitrogen-containing gas should be brown $\text{NO}_2$, not colourless $\text{NO}$, and magnesium is far too reactive to form a nitride here.
Check atom balance for Mg, N and O on both sides to pick the equation that has the right three products in the right ratio.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 2 nitrate pattern**

Think of this as a family rule you can trust. All Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating in the same way.

Chemical pattern:
$$\text{metal nitrate} \rightarrow \text{metal oxide} + \text{nitrogen dioxide} + \text{oxygen}$$

**Apply it to magnesium nitrate**

Magnesium gives $\text{MgO}$ as the solid, plus $\text{NO}_2$ (brown gas) plus $\text{O}_2$. It does not give $\text{NO}$ and it does not give a nitride like $\text{Mg}_2\text{N}_3$.

Unbalanced skeleton:
$$\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{MgO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Balance Mg, N and O**

We need 2 nitrates to give 2 oxides and 4 $\text{NO}_2$ to balance Mg and N, then 1 $\text{O}_2$ balances O. Count: 2 Mg, 4 N and 12 O on each side.

Balanced equation:
$$2\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

options.A: Atoms happen to balance, but the chemistry is wrong. Group 2 nitrates give only $\text{NO}_2$ as the nitrogen oxide, not a mixture of $\text{NO}_2$ + $\text{NO}$. This mixes up two different nitrogen oxides.
options.B: This is balanced for atoms but gives the wrong gas. $\text{NO}$ is colourless and is not the product from a Group 2 nitrate. The correct brown gas is $\text{NO}_2$.
options.C: This is correct. It shows the right three products, $\text{MgO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$, and it is fully balanced with 2 Mg, 4 N and 12 O on each side.
options.D: This is incorrect. $\text{Mg}_2\text{N}_3$ is not even a correct formula (magnesium nitride is $\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$) and nitrides are not formed by heating nitrates in air. It also uses $\text{NO}$ instead of $\text{NO}_2$.
